en.title: Salesforce OA #17: Maximum Strength Sum
en.description:
Given an integer array arr of length n, you may perform the following operation any number of times (possibly 0): choose an index i (0≤i<n−1) and swap arr[i] and arr[i+1]. Over the whole process, each element of the array may take part in at most one swap.

The strength of index i (0-based) is defined as arr[i]×(i+1). Find the maximum possible value of Σ arr[i]×(i+1) (i from 0 to n−1) after all operations.
en.input: The first line contains an integer n; the second line contains n integers arr[0..n−1], separated by whitespace. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤arr[i]≤100000.
en.output: Output one integer: the maximum strength sum.
en.explanation:
Example 1: swapping arr[2] and arr[3] gives [1,9,3,7,2], with strength sum 1×1+2×9+3×3+4×7+5×2=66.
Example 2: swapping (arr[0],arr[1]) and (arr[2],arr[3]) gives [1,2,3,4], with strength sum 30.
Example 3: no swap is needed; the strength sum is 1×1+2×2+3×5=20.
hints: Swapping two adjacent elements only changes the contributions of those two terms.
Each element can be swapped at most once, so the chosen swap pairs do not overlap.
Run dynamic programming over prefixes: the last element either stays in place or is swapped with the one before it.
